title: The Cold Extraction
premise: Marguerite Delacroix, a private security contractor who survived a training program designed to erase its graduates' pasts, receives a meeting invitation from a handler confirmed dead two years ago. Following it, she uncovers the Continuum—the network that trained and burned operatives like her—is still active, harvesting memories to build untraceable assets. With the help of Elias Ward, a defected analyst who loved her before her erasure, she must dismantle the network before it completes an extraction that would wipe her remaining memories of him. In the end, she destroys the Continuum's archive at the cost of her own records, choosing an uncertain future with Elias over the false safety of forgetting.
about_author: Ansel Amberdale is the pseudonym of a former security consultant who spent a decade advising private protection firms across Europe before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people whose professional silence costs them everything personal.

chapters.title: Invitation from the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Working a routine protection detail in Lisbon, she receives a calendar invite from Tomas Reiner, her handler who died two years ago, scheduling a meeting for tomorrow at a café she's never told anyone about. The beat is dread sharpening into reluctant curiosity; she decides to go.

chapters.title: The Café Nobody Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The meeting is a dead drop: a keycard, a partial list of Continuum operatives, and a note in Reiner's handwriting warning 'they're finishing what they started with you.' She realizes someone is using his identity. Beat: the past she buried has a pulse.

chapters.title: Sleepless Protocol
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with a flashback to the incident in Marseille that ended her sleep. She runs counter-surveillance and confirms she's being followed by someone trained the way she was. Beat: isolation—the first time she wants a partner and has no one to call.

chapters.title: The Analyst Who Waited
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A Continuum data analyst defects, carrying evidence of an operation called Cold Extraction targeting erased operatives. He searches for Marguerite, the one subject he never stopped tracking. Beat: longing constrained by tradecraft; he finds her, and she almost shoots him.

chapters.title: Terms of Contact
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Elias proves he knew her before the erasure—a name, a song, a scar she can't explain. She doesn't trust him, but she needs his access. They agree to a temporary alliance with rules neither intends to keep. Beat: wary, charged proximity.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He explains the Continuum's method: extract operative memories, repackage them as leverage, sell deniable skills. Marguerite learns her 'incident' in Marseille wasn't an accident but a test. Beat: grief and fury braided together; her trauma was a product.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her current client, a Continuum-linked financier, asks her to eliminate a 'leak'—Elias. She plays along to buy time, feeding false confirmation. Beat: love against duty made literal; she chooses him with a lie.

chapters.title: Reiner's Ghost
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Elias, alternating. They trace the dead handler's identity to a Continuum archivist, Voss, who has been resurrecting dead operatives' files to bait survivors back. Beat: the trap has an architect, and Reiner's death was the first move.

chapters.title: Safehouse, Unsafe Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Laying low in a safehouse, she and Elias share what they remember of each other—her fragments, his intact recollections. She sleeps four hours for the first time in two years. Beat: tenderness as vulnerability; belonging is a risk she's relearning.

chapters.title: The Marseille File
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He decrypts her extraction file and finds a second copy—one held by a buyer inside a European intelligence service. The Continuum isn't just selling skills; it's selling governments their own people. Beat: the conspiracy widens past survival into consequence.

chapters.title: Burn Notice, Reversed
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her client discovers her deception and marks her for extraction. She escapes an ambush using techniques she doesn't remember learning—Reiner's training surfacing like scar tissue. Beat: she is the weapon they built, and she hates how well it works.

chapters.title: The List of the Unmade
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Elias, alternating. They compile the surviving erased operatives from Reiner's list—eleven people, three still active, one already contacted by Voss. Beat: from lone survival to reluctant leadership; she starts building something like a team.

chapters.title: One of the Eleven
chapters.summary: New operative Dana Kovač's POV. Marguerite recruits Dana, a fellow erased operative, who tests her loyalty brutally before committing. Dana reveals Voss promised to restore her memories—for a price. Beat: the enemy's offer is genuinely tempting; forgetting was never consent.

chapters.title: The Price of Return
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Voss contacts her directly: help complete Cold Extraction and the Continuum will return everything Marseille took—including why she can't sleep. Beat: the devil's bargain lands at her weakest hour, and Elias watches her consider it.

chapters.title: Fracture Lines
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts Marguerite about the offer; they fight about what memory is worth and who gets to decide. She walks out. Beat: the relationship cracks under the weight of duty versus love, and both are right.

chapters.title: Double Entry
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She accepts Voss's meeting as a feint, feeding the Continuum a false extraction timeline while Dana and Elias map the archive facility beneath a Geneva clinic. Beat: cold competence masking terror; the con only works if she means it, and part of her does.

chapters.title: The Geneva Clinic
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, inside the facility. Guided in as a cooperating subject, she sees the extraction chairs, the memory vaults, her own file on a shelf. She plants the access breach and finds Reiner's final recording: he died protecting the list. Beat: grief converts to resolve.

chapters.title: Cold Extraction
chapters.summary: Climax begins, ensemble POV. The team hits the archive as Voss initiates an emergency extraction on the three active operatives—including Marguerite, strapped in before she can spring the trap. Beat: the nightmare of Marseille replaying with her awake inside it.

chapters.title: What She Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: Climax, Marguerite's POV. Mid-extraction, she must select which memories to purge to corrupt the archive—she sacrifices her records of the training and, painfully, her clearest memories of Elias, overwriting the vault with noise. Beat: love against duty resolved; she keeps the feeling and loses the evidence.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The archive burns; Voss dies trying to save a single drive; Dana and the others scatter with new identities. Elias finds Marguerite in the wreckage, unsure if she knows him. Beat: aftermath held in suspension—the question 'do you know me?' left hanging.

chapters.title: The Song He Hums
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She doesn't remember Elias, but she hums the song he once told her was theirs, and her body relaxes around him before her mind catches up. She chooses to learn him again from scratch. Beat: belonging without proof; memory rebuilt as choice rather than inheritance.

chapters.title: First Night
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue weeks later. The Continuum's remnants are being quietly dismantled by the intelligence buyer's scandal; Marguerite sleeps through the night beside Elias, and wakes—briefly unsure—then certain. Beat: resolution as earned peace; the incident is finally over.
